percentage-off is recorded here but is already subtracted from Arise.IsvApiBff.Contracts.v2.Transaction.SharedDtos.AmountDetailsDto.BaseAmount, because

component of the processed amount.

taxAmount.description:
Sales tax charged on top of Arise.IsvApiBff.Contracts.v2.Transaction.SharedDtos.AmountDetailsDto.BaseAmount, as the tip and surcharge are. Zero when

price: such a tax is inside Arise.IsvApiBff.Contracts.v2.Transaction.SharedDtos.AmountDetailsDto.BaseAmount and reporting it here as well would count

Rate behind Arise.IsvApiBff.Contracts.v2.Transaction.SharedDtos.AmountDetailsDto.TaxAmount, as a percent (e.g. 10 = 10%); zero under the same rule.
It describes the base the tax was computed on, which for a resource that taxes a narrower base
than the transaction amount — an invoice taxing only its line items — is not

ApplicationDeliveryMethod.description:
How the application link reaches the merchant.

Possible values:

  • 1 - Email: We email the merchant an invitation carrying the link; applicationUrl is returned as well.
  • 2 - PartnerDirect: Nothing is sent. You deliver applicationUrl to the merchant yourself.
  • 3 - Iframe: Nothing is sent. You embed applicationUrl in an iframe on your own page; the merchant completes and signs the application there without creating a Flute account. The frame posts two messages to your page, each with { type, applicationId }: flute:application-submitted when the merchant submits, and flute:application-signed when the frame returns from signing. Check that event.origin matches the origin of applicationUrl before acting on a message, and treat the messages as a cue to refresh your UI rather than as the application's state: the webhooks and GET /v2/applications remain the source of truth. The frame navigates to the signing provider and back, so do not sandbox it in a way that blocks navigation or scripts.

ApplicationStatus.description:
Where a merchant application currently stands. A small, stable vocabulary giving a high-level view of the application's lifecycle; the application lifecycle webhooks report the individual events that move it between these states.

Possible values:

  • 1 - InProgress: Started but not yet submitted, whether by the merchant (including signing) or by a partner or agent on their behalf.
  • 2 - InReview: Submitted and under review. No additional information is currently required from the merchant.
  • 3 - InformationNeeded: Additional information or documents are required from the merchant before the review can continue.
  • 4 - Rejected: Declined; the application will not move forward.
  • 5 - AutoDeclined: Automatically declined because the merchant did not respond to an information request in time.
  • 6 - Active: Approved; the merchant is able to process payments.
  • 7 - Cancelled: Withdrawn or removed before completion.
  • 8 - Draft: Created by the partner; the merchant has not been invited to it yet.

CreatePosReversalRequestDto.description:
Request to create a reversal from POS. With `originalTransactionId` the backend picks the
execution path: a void when still available, a referenced refund in the cloud for credit cards
(both without a terminal flow), or a refund flow on the terminal for debit cards (the customer
presents the card). Without it, an unreferenced refund flow is initiated on the terminal.

ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., "USD", "EUR", "GBP") | Conditional — mandatory for
unreferenced refunds.

See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217

The transaction to reverse | Optional. When omitted, an unreferenced refund is initiated
on the terminal.

referenceId.description: External Transaction Reference ID | Mandatory | MaxLength=36

reversalAmount.description:
Amount to reverse | Conditional — mandatory for unreferenced refunds (no
`originalTransactionId`); caps a partial refund for referenced reversals.
Ignored when the reversal resolves to a void (voids reverse the full amount).

terminalId.description:
Terminal ID related to the terminal that handles the refund flow. Terminal must be in the
semi-integrated mode; Cloud-channel refund flows additionally require it to be available
(online and ready).

waitForAcceptanceByTerminal.description:
Set the response mode to short or long polling for terminal refund flows.


If ```true``` (long polling): HTTP response will be provided once the terminal accepts/declines to initiate the refund or a timeout happens (terminal does not respond).


If ```false``` (short polling): HTTP response will be returned immediately, while the terminal is still receiving the refund request.


Reversals that resolve to a void or a credit-card refund complete in the cloud and respond synchronously regardless of this flag.

See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_4217

waitForAcceptanceByTerminal.description:
Set the response mode to short or long polling.


If ```true``` (long polling): HTTP response will be provided once the terminal accepts/declines to initiate the transaction or a timeout happens (terminal does not respond). Follow-up calls to get the POS Transaction By ID should be done to retrieve the latest information of the transaction submission.


If ```false``` (short polling): HTTP response will be returned immediately, while the terminal is still receiving the transaction request. Follow-up calls to get the POS Transaction By ID should be done to retrieve the latest information of the transaction initiation and submission.

securityCode.description: The three or four digit security code on the card.

taxAmount.description:
Tax the transaction was quoted at, whatever the mode. It describes the quote, as the amount
breakdown does: a capture or a host approval for less leaves it unchanged, and processedAmount
reports what was taken.

taxRate.description:
The rate the tax was configured at, as a percent (e.g. 8.5 = 8.5%). A resource that supplies its
own tax amount — an invoice, which taxes its line items rather than the whole amount — has this
rate recorded rather than applied, so it need not reproduce Arise.IsvApiBff.Contracts.v2.Transaction.SharedDtos.TaxDetailsDto.TaxAmount; one that
supplies only the amount has the rate derived from it.

taxableAmount.description:
What the quote charged before the tax: its total less the tip, the surcharge and an Exclusive tax,
all charged outside the taxed amount, and less Arise.IsvApiBff.Contracts.v2.Transaction.SharedDtos.TaxDetailsDto.TaxAmount when the tax is Inclusive
and therefore already inside it. With a rate-driven tax this is the amount the rate was applied
to, to the cent: the quote's components are each rounded before they are stored, so the residual
can differ from it by 0.01. With a supplied amount it is still what was charged before tax, which
is not the narrower base that amount was computed on.

TipAdjustmentRequestDto.description:
Request to adjust the tip on a card transaction. Provide exactly one of
Arise.IsvApiBff.Contracts.v2.Transaction.Requests.TipAdjustmentRequestDto.TipAmount or Arise.IsvApiBff.Contracts.v2.Transaction.Requests.TipAdjustmentRequestDto.TipRate.

tipAmount.description: Tip as a fixed amount. Mutually exclusive with Arise.IsvApiBff.Contracts.v2.Transaction.Requests.TipAdjustmentRequestDto.TipRate.

tipRate.description:
Tip as a percent of the transaction's base amount (e.g. 15 = 15%); the gateway integrates
it into the merchant's pricing formula. Mutually exclusive with Arise.IsvApiBff.Contracts.v2.Transaction.Requests.TipAdjustmentRequestDto.TipAmount.

dutyChargesRate.description: Import or export duties on the order as a percentage rate (e.g. 2.5 = 2.5%). Must be between 0 and 100.

invoiceNumber.description:

Between 1 and 15 characters; letters, numbers and spaces only.

purchaseOrder.description: The value used by the customer to identify an order. Issued by the buyer to the seller.

salesTaxRate.description: Sales tax rate as a percentage between 0 and 100. Also limited to 4 characters by the TSYS field width (e.g. 8.25 / 99.9).

shippingCharges.description: The dollar amount for shipping or freight charges applied to a product or transaction. Must be 0 or greater.

amount.description: The requested amount for the operation.

originalTransactionId.description: On Refund events, the id of the refund transaction created by the event.

transaction.

across payments.

value.description: The answer as plain text, exactly as entered.

discountRate.description: The discount percentage applied to a product. This does not impact transaction functionality. It is used for reporting purposes. Must be between 0 and 100.

measurementUnit.description: The unit of measurement for the product. Between 1 and 20 characters; letters, numbers and spaces only.

productCode.description: The merchant's assigned unique product identification code. Between 1 and 20 characters.

productName.description: The name of the product. Between 1 and 50 characters.

quantity.description: The quantity of a product. Must be greater than zero.

taxAmount.description: The tax amount established on a product.

unitPrice.description: The price per product unit. Must be greater than zero.

omitted field is left unchanged while an explicit null clears it. The exception is the state:
moving the address to US requires sending stateCode, and moving it out of US clears stateCode
when it is not sent.

countryCode.description: Country code in ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 format (e.g., "US", "CA", "GB").

stateCode.description:
ISO 3166-2 subdivision code. For US states, the USPS two-letter abbreviation
is used (e.g., "NY", "CA", "TX").

field. An id that does not belong to this link is rejected.

isRequired.description:
true: the customer must answer before paying. false: the field is shown as optional and can
be left empty.

name.description:

such as tabs or line breaks. Duplicate names are allowed.

UpdatePaymentLinkRequestDto.description:
JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) body for a payment link. An omitted field is left unchanged;
an explicit `null` clears a clearable field.

baseAmount.description:
Payment amount, must be greater than 0 when provided. Explicit null = flexible amount
(the customer enters it at checkout).

currencyCode.description:
ISO 4217 uppercase currency code. Cannot be cleared, and the currency is frozen once
the link has received payments.

customerId.description:
Customer the link is issued for. Explicit null detaches the customer; the link's mode
stays as it is. On a MultiUse link its payments, and any payment method a payer saves
there, are recorded under this customer, but the payment page never shows the
customer's details or saved methods.

description.description: Merchant-internal notes, max 500 characters. Explicit null clears them.

expiresOn.description: UTC expiration; must be a future date. Explicit null = the link never expires.

extraFields.description:
Replaces the whole list; arrays are not merged. Include an extraFieldId to keep that field,
leave it out for a new field. An empty list or explicit null removes every field. Only
sessions the link opens afterwards carry the change.

metadata.description:
Merged key by key: a key with a value is added or replaced, a key set to null is removed,
and keys left out are kept. Explicit null removes every key. The merged pairs must stay
within the limits of create. Only sessions the link opens afterwards carry the change.

name.description: Merchant-facing label, max 80 characters. Cannot be cleared.

referenceId.description: Merchant label, max 200 characters. Explicit null clears it.

taxAmount.description:

rule as taxRate; the merged link must keep a fixed baseAmount, and in Inclusive mode the
amount must stay below it.

Every leaf field is RiseOsV2.Rest.MergePatch.Optional`1 and the nested groups are themselves
field-level optional, so patching one nested field leaves its siblings intact.

Default sale tax rate. Must be between 0 and 22.
Encoded as raw percentage — e.g. 8.5 represents 8.5%.

dutyChargeRate.description:

Encoded as raw percentage — e.g. 2.5 represents 2.5%.

shippingChargeRate.description:
The percentage for shipping or freight charges applied to a product or transaction.
Encoded as raw percentage — e.g. 2.5 represents 2.5%.

discountRate.description: Product discount rate. Encoded as raw percentage — e.g. 10 represents 10%.

measurementUnit.description: The unit of measurement for the product.

productCode.description: The merchant assigned unique product identification code.

A person who can sign in under your partner account, one of your merchants, or an application
you invited. One row per person, however many of those accounts they hold a profile on.

Which account a user belongs to.

Possible values:

  • 1 - Partner: A user of your partner account.
  • 2 - Merchant: A user of one of your merchants.
  • 3 - Applicant: A merchant applicant you invited, still working through their application.

WalletPaymentMethodDto.description:
A digital wallet (Apple Pay, Google Pay) offered on a payment session. Wallets are card-network
wallets: the payment authorizes as a card payment on the session's card processor. Whether a
session offers a wallet follows from the merchant's wallet enablement, the card processor and
the merchant's pricing mode, so it is reported on reads and not configured per session.

post.description:
Invites a merchant to complete an application you have pre-filled. Send as little as the
business name and the merchant's email, or as much of the application as you hold; every
field you leave out stays empty for the merchant to fill in, including sensitive ones such
as SSN and bank details. The application is attributed to partnerUserId, whose feeScheduleId
and splitProfileId must be among the ones GET /v2/users/{userId}/fee-schedules and
GET /v2/users/{userId}/split-profiles return for that user. List the owners in owners, at most 4, principal owner first.
deliveryMethod decides who hands the merchant the link: Email means
we send the invitation email; PartnerDirect means you deliver applicationUrl yourself; Iframe
means you embed applicationUrl in an iframe on your own page and the merchant completes and
signs the application there without creating a Flute account; the frame posts
flute:application-submitted and flute:application-signed to your page as it goes, and your page
should check event.origin against applicationUrl before acting on them. The link grants access to the
application, so treat it like a password. Send an Idempotency-Key to make retries safe, and
metadata to correlate the application with your own records; it is stored as sent and
returned on the response and on GET /v2/applications. The response is the created
application, as GET /v2/applications/{applicationId} returns it, plus applicationUrl and
deliveryMethod; applicationUrl is returned only here.

Server errors (5xx) are not stored: retrying the same key after one executes the request again.

post.description:
Each `paymentMethods[]` item carries a `paymentMethodType` of `Card` or `ACH` and only that
type's fields: a Card needs `cardNumber`, `securityCode`, `expirationMonth` and
`expirationYear`; an ACH account needs `accountRoutingNumber`, `accountNumber`,
`accountHolderType` and `accountType`, plus `taxId` when `accountHolderType` is `Business`
(which also makes the customer's `companyName` required). Every item needs a
`paymentMethodName` of at most 20 characters. `externalId` (at most 100 characters) can be
set only here, on create. `hasSmsConsent` defaults to false. `shippingAddress` is ignored
while `shouldUseBillingAsShippingAddress` is true. Address limits: `postalCode` 5 to 10
characters, `city` at most 50, each address line at most 200. Returns the full created
customer, with `paymentMethods` oldest first. Answers `403` unless the token carries the
`ManageCustomers` permission; a partner token is refused.
            
With an ACH item, `billingAddress` is required and must be one the account can be charged against:
            
- `countryCode`: `US`
- `stateCode`: required, a US state
- `city`: required
- `addressLine1`: required, at most 70 characters
- `addressLine2`: at most 40 characters
- `postalCode`: required, a ZIP code (`#####` or `#####-####`)
